title: Content chunking for long memories
summary: Split long content into embedded chunks at write time so a 64KB memory gets more than one (diluted) embedding; search resolves chunk hits back to parent records.
description:
For content exceeding a configurable threshold (e.g. > 2000 characters), split it into overlapping chunks at write time and embed each chunk separately, instead of the current one-embedding-per-row-no-matter-how-long-the-content approach (a 64KB CLOB today gets a single embedding, which is a poor semantic representation of the whole text). Add a new companion table (e.g. `memory_chunks`: `id`, `source_table`, `source_id`, `chunk_index`, `chunk_text`, `embedding VECTOR(...) NOT NULL`, scope columns for isolation, `CREATE VECTOR INDEX`) via a new migration. `create()`/`update()` in `repositories/base.py` gain chunking logic gated by the length threshold — short content behaves exactly as today (single embedding on the parent row; no chunk rows created). Add a `search(..., search_chunks=True)` mode that searches `memory_chunks` first (finer-grained semantic match against chunk text) then resolves and dedupes back to parent records, ranked by each parent's best-matching chunk distance.

Inspired by: Oracle AI Agent Memory's `APP_MEMORY_RECORD_CHUNKS` table — content is chunked for retrieval rather than embedding one giant blob as a single vector.

Db2 feasibility: feasible, but the largest-scope item in this epic — a new table + index per existing table (or one shared chunks table, your call, justify whichever in DECISIONS.md), new chunking utility code, and search() branching logic. No new infrastructure beyond what Step 2 already established (another VECTOR NOT NULL column + CREATE VECTOR INDEX, same pattern).

comments.text: Done. Added shared memory_chunks table (migration 0006) with VECTOR(1536,FLOAT32) NOT NULL embedding, source_table/source_id discriminator, chunk_index, scope columns, CREATE VECTOR INDEX (COSINE), and two supporting indexes. _split_chunks() sliding-window utility in repositories/base.py (chunk_size=800, chunk_overlap=200, configurable). BaseRepository gains chunk_repo/chunk_threshold/chunk_size/chunk_overlap constructor args and _write_chunks() helper; create() and update() gate on (chunk_repo is not None AND embedding_provider is not None AND len(content) > threshold) — below threshold behaves identically to pre-ORC-2. Parent row's embedding gets zero-vector sentinel when chunked (NOT NULL satisfied; semantic representation lives in memory_chunks). ChunkRepository (repositories/chunks.py) provides insert_chunk(), delete_by_source(), search_chunks() — two-step rank+resolve pattern for Db2 12.1.5 fp0 VECTOR_SERIALIZE compatibility. search(search_chunks=True) in BaseRepository routes to _search_via_chunks(): step 1 over-fetch chunks (top_k×4), step 2 dedup to best distance per source_id, step 3 resolve + re-rank parents. MemoryStore gains embedding_provider, enable_chunking, chunk_threshold, chunk_size, chunk_overlap constructor args; when embedding_provider is supplied it builds one shared ChunkRepository and injects it into all five per-type repos along with the provider. Backward compat: no embedding_provider → chunk_repo=None → pre-ORC-2 code path. 41 new unit tests, 445 total passing. ruff clean. DECISIONS.md + ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 updated.
